title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The base is S_0 = Spec Z[1/2]. A 'Legendre-Jacobi pinning' (épinglage) of an elliptic curve E/S is, roughly, an ordering of the three non-trivial 2-torsion points plus a normalisation of coordinates bringing E to the form y^2 = x(x-1)(x-λ), or to the Jacobi form. The normalisation also produces a section of μ_4^× (a primitive 4th root of unity), so the moduli scheme of pinned curves is U_{0,3} × μ_4^×, where U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,∞} is the λ-line. The group S_3 × μ_4 acts on this scheme: S_3 tautologically (permuting 0, 1, ∞, i.e. the anharmonic group on λ) and μ_4 by rescaling. The previous page computed the action on the factor μ_4^× (a μ_2-torsor) through the mixed character sg(g)·ζ^2.

The group D'_3. The stabiliser of μ_4^× is D'_3 = S_3 ×_{Z/2} Z/4, a central extension of S_3 by {±1}. This group has order 12. It is Z/3 ⋊ Z/4, the dicyclic (binary dihedral) group Dic_3, whose abelianisation is Z/4. That abelianisation is the χ_4 of the next page.

This page, first step: base change to S~_0 = μ_4^× over S_0, i.e. Z[1/2, i] with i fixed.
- Call a pinning 'direct' if the section of μ_4^× it defines equals the chosen i.
- For relative elliptic curves over S/S~_0, the functor of direct Legendre-Jacobi pinnings is represented by U_{0,3} over S~_0.
- The 'modular group' acting on this moduli scheme is D'_3. It is exactly the subgroup of D_3 × μ_4 that sends direct pinnings to direct pinnings.
- So the modular group of the level-2 Legendre moduli is enlarged from S_3 to its central extension by the automorphism -1 of the curve. This makes U_{0,3} over S~_0 an honest fine moduli scheme instead of a μ_2-gerbe.

This page, second step: return to the base S_0 and make explicit the action of μ_4 × S_3 on the line bundle O(1) pulled back to U_{0,3} × μ_4^×.
- O(1) is the tautological bundle of P(V_{0,1,∞}(O_{S_0})), the rank-2 module on which S_3 acts tautologically.
- S_3 acts through this tautological action, and μ_4 through its action on the factor μ_4^×.
- For (g,λ), the tautological ('canonical substitution') action on a section ξ of O(1) over t: S → M_{0,3} is denoted (g,λ).ξ.

Next page. The modular action is compared with the tautological one:
- T_{g,λ}ξ = λ (g,λ).ξ on O(1).
- λ^2 on O(2).
- λ^2 sg(g) on a twisted O(2).
- Restricting to D'_3, where λ^2 = sg(g), these become: χ_4(g) on O(1), the sign on O(2), and trivial on the twisted O(2).

Purpose: an explicit description of the line bundle of modular forms on the level-2 / Legendre moduli and of its equivariance under the finite modular group. The aim is to descend from the level-2 cover (λ-line) to the level-1 moduli stack M_{1,1} over Z[1/2], i.e. to present M_{1,1}[1/2] as [U_{0,3}/D'_3] with an explicit description of the bundle of modular forms in terms of O(1).
errors: No mathematical error visible on this page. The identification of the stabiliser of directness with D'_3 = S_3 ×_{Z/2} Z/4 agrees with the kernel of sg(g)·ζ^2 computed on the previous page, and its abelianisation is indeed Z/4.

Minor imprecision: in the line 'est représentable par U_{03}S~_0' the base should be read as U_{0,3} × S~_0 (i.e. U_{0,3} over S~_0). Also the relative-base insertion '(sur des S/S_0)' should probably read S/S~_0, since directness needs the fixed i.

ideas.what: Legendre-Jacobi pinning (level-2 structure plus Legendre/Jacobi normalisation) over Z[1/2] as a rigidification of the moduli of elliptic curves; the moduli scheme is U_{0,3} × μ_4^×.
ideas.modern_name: Legendre family / full level-2 structure with rigidification; M(2) over Z[1/2] ≅ λ-line
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre, Jacobi); scheme-theoretic treatment in Igusa, Deligne-Rapoport (1973), Katz-Mazur (1985)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1} and M_{0,4} and the Teichmüller tower in general terms, but not this explicit pinning, as far as I know

ideas.what: The modular group of direct pinnings over Z[1/2, i] is D'_3 = S_3 ×_{Z/2} Z/4, a central extension of S_3 by ±1 (the dicyclic group of order 12), acting on U_{0,3}. So M_{1,1}[1/2, i] ≅ [U_{0,3}/D'_3].
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of M_{1,1} as a quotient stack [M(2)/SL_2(Z/2)-extension]; binary dihedral group Dic_3 as a quotient of SL_2(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; cf. Deligne-Rapoport and the standard presentation M_{1,1}[1/2] = [(A^2 - Δ)/G_m] or [M(2)/GL_2(F_2)]

ideas.what: Explicit equivariant structure of O(1) on the λ-line under S_3 × μ_4. The modular action differs from the tautological one by the character λ^k sg(g)^ε. Restricted to D'_3, weight 1 carries χ_4, O(2) carries the sign, and the twisted O(2) is invariant.
ideas.modern_name: Modular forms of level 2 as sections of O(k) on P^1 with explicit S_3-equivariant (character-twisted) linearisation; theta-constant description
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (theta constants, Igusa); modern treatments of M_{1,1} via level 2, e.g. Mumford's Picard group of the moduli problem and Fulton-Olsson

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, explicit scheme-theoretic bookkeeping of the Legendre/Jacobi level-2 moduli over Z[1/2] and its finite modular group. The identification of that group with the dicyclic group S_3 ×_{Z/2} Z/4 and the character-twisted linearisation of O(1) are classical or folklore. Nothing here is beyond what Deligne-Rapoport, Katz-Mazur or later stack-theoretic treatments contain.
